ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening of all UBOs, shareholders, directors, and major counterparties against (i) TRACFIN typology reports, (ii) EU restrictive measures and asset-freezing lists (Council Regulation 269/2014 and DG Trésor national freezing decisions), (iii) UN Security Council sanctions, (iv) the French national freezing list, and (v) OFAC SDN as best practice for USD clearing via documentary letters of credit. Screening is repeated at KYC onboarding, at each significant transaction, and on alert-driven review; obligations are anchored in Articles L.561-5 and L.561-6 CMF and TRACFIN's declarations to the Procureur de la République; enhanced monitoring applies because the recycled-scrap stream is classified as a medium-risk circular-metals activity with high counterparty diversity.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.regulatory_license_flag: true — the activity of purchasing, trading and consigning waste metals falls within the French regulated regime of négociant en déchets under Articles L.541-7 and R.541-42 et seq. of the Code de l'environnement, requiring pre-incorporation representation in the Trackdéchets system and DREAL/Préfecture notification or registration prior to first transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises operated by INPI (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr); name and trademark availability search via data.inpi.fr and infogreffe.fr; consolidated national register is the Registre National des Entreprises (RNE) with RCS extraction by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All RCS and RNE file data must be submitted in French; any foreign-language corporate name or supporting document requires sworn translation by an approved expert translator. The dénomination sociale may be a coined term or foreign name provided it is rendered in Latin-script characters, is clearly distinguishable from prior RNE registrations, does not mislead the public, and is not contrary to ordre public or bonnes moeurs.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not operate a statutory pre-filing name reservation; priority is obtained either by the INPI trademark filing (effective from filing date) or by the effective RNE registration. If the Guichet Unique rejects the incorporation file due to identity or confusing similarity with an existing dénomination, the applicant must re-file with an amended name, or contest the refusal before the Président du tribunal de commerce under Article L.123-5-6 of the Code de commerce, and, for trademark disputes, use the INPI opposition and nullity procedures under Articles L.712-4, L.712-7 and L.716-1 of the Code de la propriété intellectuelle. The 30-day value in this dossier reflects the internal hold period applied during final availability verification before submission of the incorporation file.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible with restrictions. A virtual office is lawful under the regulated domiciliation regime (Articles L.123-11-2 and R.123-11-2 of the Code de commerce; Décret n°2011-646) for a maximum period of five years, subject to a formal domiciliation agreement and registration with the greffe. For this activity (cross-border consignment trading without French stock), a domiciliation address is accepted for the RCS file, but the DREAL/Préfecture waste-dealer registration requires full disclosure of any French or foreign operational and storage sites; a pure trading desk without national territory stock may operate from the domiciliation address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Elevated: 35 to 50% probability of an unannounced on-site control within the first 12 to 24 months by TRACFIN, French Customs (DGDDI), or DREAL inspectors under Article L.171-1 of the Code de l'environnement, driven by the ICPE-classified metals waste stream, the medium-risk AML tier, and the use of documentary credit/TT payment rails with non-resident suppliers.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP), Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty. Professional portal: impots.gouv.fr. Company registration gateway: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (INPI sole door for company formalities in France). Non-resident VAT desk: Service des Impôts des Non-Résidents (SINR), 10 rue du Centre, 93460 Noisy-le-Grand. EU VAT number validation: VIES (https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: For a French SAS, incorporation is filed through the INPI one-stop shop (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr), triggering issuance of the SIREN (9-digit national registry number) and SIRET within 3-5 business days. Step 2: DGFiP automatically allocates the French intra-Community VAT number in the format FR + 2-digit key + 9-digit SIREN; the VAT certificate is retrievable via the company's professional account on impots.gouv.fr. Step 3: For a non-established foreign seller, a formal VAT registration application (Cerfa n° 12855, 'Immatriculation d'un assujetti non établi') is filed with the SINR, attaching the foreign commercial registry extract, proof of foreign VAT status, and, for non-EU applicants, a mandatory fiscal representation mandate (Article 289 A CGI, approved representative). Registration is acknowledged within 15 business days and completed in approximately 5 weeks; the VAT number is effective on issuance. Step 4: For operations subject to domestic reverse charge (waste/scrap), the French client is itself liable for VAT remittance; the non-resident supplier still requires a French VAT ID if it is carrying on a permanent revenue-generating activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope_France / No_Tax_Exempt_Zone. An SAS is by default fully subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) under Articles 206 and 209 CGI, on worldwide profits when its registered office or place of effective management is in France. Standard CIT rate: 25% for fiscal years opened from 1 January 2022. No pass-through treatment is available to an SAS. Metropolitan France offers no general tax-exempt zone for industrial/commercial activity; tax advantages are limited to specified overseas territories (Guyane, Mayotte) and incentive regimes not applicable to the base profile.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style 'check-the-box' election exists. Statutory election levers: (i) French fiscal group integration (Article 223 A CGI) for subsidiaries held at 95% or more, enabling consolidated CIT settlement; (ii) VAT group registration ('assujetti unique', Article 256 C CGI), allowing group VAT consolidation among closely aligned French entities; (iii) hybrid-mismatch alignment under Article 202 C CGI and the French ATAD transposition: taxpayers may obtain a binding legal ruling (rescrit fiscal) to align the French tax classification of a foreign hybrid entity and neutralize deduction/non-inclusion mismatches; (iv) the regime of tax-transparent partnerships (régime des sociétés de personnes, Article 239 A CGI) is not available to an SAS; (v) for certain small companies, an option can be made to remain within the individual income tax regime (Article 239 B CGI) solely in the formation period, but this is strictly limited and incompatible with an SAS used for cross-border trading. Elections are filed with the local SIE before the end of the relevant fiscal year and are irrevocable for the chosen duration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.mandatory_digital_fiscal_identity: Every French SAS is required to hold a valid SIRET and intra-Community VAT number before issuing tax-compliant invoices. The 'Identifiant TVA' must be shown on invoices (Article 242 nonies A, annexe II CGI). For e-invoicing, the company must register on the Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or contract with a registered Partner Dematerialization Platform (PDP); a single 'numéro d'immatriculation PPF' is allocated to each taxable person.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: TVA (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée) — Value Added Tax, harmonized under EU Directive 2006/112/EC and codified in Articles 256 to 289 quinquies of the French General Tax Code (CGI).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: The general small-business VAT exemption (franchise en base, Article 293 B CGI) applies up to EUR 91,900 of turnover for supplies of goods (2025) and EUR 36,800 for services. However, supplies of non-ferrous scrap, waste and recoverable materials (including shredded copper wire) are excluded from the franchise and are mandatorily subject to VAT, with the domestic reverse-charge mechanism (Article 283-2 CGI) making the French customer liable for VAT. Consequently, the effective registration threshold for this business is EUR 0: every French SAS trading in scrap copper wire must be VAT-registered from the first transaction. A EUR 10,000 annual intra-EU distance-sales threshold applies for sales to private consumers in other Member States; B2B supplies are governed by the place-of-supply rules of Articles 258 and 258 A CGI.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is rolling out a mandatory B2B e-invoicing and e-reporting framework without a real-time fiscal clearance stamp. Timeline: from 1 September 2026, all taxable persons established in France must be able to receive e-invoices, and large/mid-size businesses must issue e-invoices; from 1 September 2027, small and micro enterprises must also issue e-invoices. Mandatory formats: Factur-X (EN 16931 hybrid), UBL 2.1, or CII. Invoices are transmitted through the free public platform PPF (Portail Public de Facturation) or a certified PDP; transaction and payment data are e-reported to DGFiP via the PPF within 10 days of invoice issuance. B2G invoicing is already mandatory on the Chorus Pro platform. For international B2B transactions, e-reporting of sales and payment data applies; the duty to transmit applies to the supplier. There is no digital stamping, continuous fiscal sealing (socle), or pre-clearance authorization system at the national level; DGFiP applies automated data analytics and cross-checks against customs declarations (DELTA) and bank payment data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export deliveries of goods are exempt with right to deduction/refund pursuant to Article 262-I-1° CGI and BOI-TVA-EXP-30-10. Claim conditions: (i) the supply transfers the right to dispose of the goods; (ii) the goods are physically shipped or transported outside the European Union by the seller, on the seller's behalf, or — in the framework of a chain supply — the EX-PAYS/EX-1 export customs declaration proves exit from EU territory; (iii) the goods leave the EU within 90 days of the supply (extension possible with valid justification); (iv) the seller retains the customs export declaration (DAU) and transport documentation consigning the copper scrap wire to a non-EU destination; (v) the buyer is identified and the commercial invoice states the applicable exemption. Non-ferrous scrap copper wire (HS 7404) qualifies as tangible goods for VAT purposes; the goods may transit through a customs warehouse before exit without breaking the zero-rating chain. Zero-rating does not require prior authorization but is subject to post-export audit substantiation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration Unique d'Exportation, DAU) — digital EX-1 document lodged via the DELTA-X customs system, validated with the MRN (Movement Reference Number) and evidencing the HS 7404 product, weight and exit office.
Bill of Lading — original negotiable ocean B/L, CMR waybill or multimodal transport document showing the consignee outside the EU and the port/place of actual exit, dated within 90 days of supply.

Inward Remittance Certificate — bank credit evidence (SWIFT MT103 / account statement) demonstrating receipt of the export proceeds in the French exporter's account, aligned with Article 913 of the French Monetary and Financial Code.
Commercial Invoice — issued without VAT, referencing Article 262-I-1° CGI and stating 'Exportation hors Union Européenne – TVA non applicable'. Must match weight, grade and value of the copper scrap.
Supplier Purchase Documents and Weighboridge Ticket (pèse-billet) — evidencing the chain of custody of the shredded copper wire from acquisition to shipment and supporting the scrap classification.
Transport and Insurance Contracts — delivery order, transit declaration (e.g., T1/community transit consignment note) and cargo insurance policy naming the French exporter as insured.
Weight and Quality Certificate — sworn assay/laboratory certificate of copper purity at the Port d'embarquement, essential for customs valuation and ISIC 4669 consistency.
Intrastat / STATLINES Declaration — where exit involves intra-EU movement prior to final non-EU export, the Intrastat statement and customs event history must be retained in the audit file.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP scrutinizes export files through a dedicated risk-scoring engine comparing customs MRN data, commercial invoices, transport waybills and bank MT103 messages. A claim of export zero-rating that is not substantiated results in forced re-invoicing of 20% VAT under Article 269 CGI plus late-payment interest (0.2% per month, Article 1727 CGI). Where the insufficiency is deemed a maneuver frauduleuse or abuse of right, a penalty of 80% of the tax due applies under Articles 1729 and 1729-0-1 CGI. Criminal sanctions under the French Customs Code (Articles 414 and 415) reach fines of up to five times the value of the goods, confiscation of the cargo or means of transport, and imprisonment of up to 10 years for organized smuggling. Company directors and de facto officers, as well as the SAS itself, are jointly and severally liable for the tax, penalties and fines (Articles 267 quinquies CGI and 1742 CGI). Fraudulent zero-rating may additionally trigger loss or suspension of fiscal clean status, refusal of the OEA (AEO) customs authorization, delisting from the recycler authorized-tax regime, and reporting to the French interbank AML unit (Tracfin) in cases covered by the Medium-Risk_Enhanced AML classification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting as central bank and balance-of-payments reporting agent; foreign exchange regulatory oversight is exercised with the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) and the ACPR (Prudential Supervision and Resolution Authority)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is an EU/OECD member and part of the eurozone; the euro is fully convertible for current-account and capital-account operations under the free movement of capital principle of the TFEU. No exchange controls apply to ordinary trade, profit remittance, or capital movements. Profit and dividend outbound transfers are permitted for legally established entities, subject to beneficial-ownership verification, anti-money-laundering/CFT screening, and tax reporting obligations. There is no mandatory conversion of export receipts and no prior administrative authorisation for standard commercial payments, except statistical reporting obligations to Banque de France for large cross-border transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: French law imposes no export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio; exporters may retain foreign currency balances in authorised foreign-currency accounts through intermediary banks. However, export receipts must comply with EU wire-transfer transparency rules (Regulation (EU) 2015/847), cash declarations above EUR 10,000 under the Customs and Monetary Code, and Banque de France balance-of-payments statistical declaration where applicable. Documentary records of the underlying purchase order, invoice, bill of lading, and customs declaration must be kept for at least 10 years.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low. ACPR-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) can open payment accounts and process SWIFT MT103 inbound/outbound wires, but they generally cannot provide documentary letters of credit, capital-escrow accounts, or comprehensive trade-finance products needed for recycled scrap copper import settlement. EMIs are subject to the EU E-Money Directive and French Monetary and Financial Code restrictions: they may not take deposits or perform credit/lending operations, and client funds must be safeguarded in regulated accounts. For a recycling trading vehicle, an EMI is viable only as a supplementary collection/disbursement rail, not as the primary clearing infrastructure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French commercial banks do not impose a blanket statutory requirement for physical presence, but in practice non-resident SAS directors are often required to complete an in-person KYC interview at the banking branch or a notarised appointment via a French consulate and apostilled documentation. Remote onboarding is permitted using video identification and biometric cross-checking under the bank's risk-based procedures, especially for low- to medium-risk clients. For a medium-risk metals-scrap trading company, banks generally apply enhanced due diligence and may still request a physical or a remote compliance committee interview before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner opacity or nominee shareholding structures
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extract from the French Trade Registry (Kbis), constitutional documents of the SAS, shareholding registry, French UBO declaration, passport copies, proof of residential address, and a corporate structure chart showing the direct and ultimate beneficial owners with a clean sanctions search result.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction or sanctioned counterparty in the scrap copper supply chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative sanctions-screen reports, country-of-origin certificates, supplier due-diligence files, export licences from the origin country, end-user declarations, shipping and customs documentation, and contractual warranty clauses confirming the supplier has no exposure to EU/OFAC sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for capital injection or shareholder loan
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or certified financial statements for the capital provider, bank reference letter, formal share purchase or loan agreement, board resolution approving the injection, tax-residence certificate, notarised signature of the beneficial owner, and a statement of purpose confirming deployment for operating capital and trade settlements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk goods classification for recycled scrap copper and variable transaction amounts
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Recycler/intermediate supplier licence, ISO 9001 quality-management certificates, chain-of-custody records, copper-grading certificates, weight certificates from independent inspectors, transaction ledger, and invoices with HS code 7404 that reconcile to physical shipping documents.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections are routed by SWIFT MT103 wire from the shareholder's bank to the SAS's euro-denominated operational account. The wire must carry a clear balance-of-payments purpose code (e.g., capital contribution or shareholder subordinated loan) and remitter description matching the shareholder name on file. The receiving French bank will verify the beneficiary IBAN, BIC/SWIFT, legal entity name, and corporate KYC pack; for larger capital movements, the resident agent bank is responsible for monthly balance-of-payments reporting to Banque de France, including the transaction value, country of the counterparty, and purpose classification. No French exchange-control authorisation is required, but documentary evidence such as a board resolution, share transfer agreement, and shareholding structure must be retained.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements are executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfers and documentary letters of credit. For commercial letters of credit, the French bank issues a revocable or, preferably, irrevocable LC under UCP 600, payable against presentation of the commercial invoice, packed list, bill of lading, certificate of origin, quality certificate, and weight certificate. Documentary collection under URC 522 is also available for stable counterparties. For direct SWIFT MT103 payments, the remitter must provide the customs export declaration, purchase order, invoice, and transport documents, and the payment field must contain the correct trade purpose code. Euro-denominated settlements avoid currency conversion; non-euro settlements are hedged according to the approved FX policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward (EUR/USD, EUR/CNY) matched to firm commercial receipts or payment obligations
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for illiquid or restricted-convertibility currencies solely to hedge underlying commodity exposure
Cross-currency interest-rate swap to hedge balance-sheet intercompany borrowings denominated in foreign currency
Currency option purchased to protect against adverse exchange-rate movements for scheduled capital repayments or major purchase contracts
FX swap structure (spot purchase with simultaneous forward sale) for short-term liquidity management

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts approval by shareholders or the competent body specified in the SAS articles
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company shareholders or other body designated by the SAS articles; no government filing for approval itself
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within six months after the financial year-end; the articles govern the decision procedure
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A court may order the company and its legal representative to complete approval; directors may face civil liability for resulting loss.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and required management or auditor reports deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry (greffe), through the French business formalities one-stop shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The president of the commercial court may issue an order to file, potentially subject to a periodic penalty. Non-filing may also result in a civil fine; non-filing alone does not automatically dissolve or strike off the company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and required schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Directorate General of Public Finances (DGFiP)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after financial year-end, or by the second working day after 1 May for a calendar-year company, subject to the applicable electronic-filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, increased in specified circumstances, plus late-payment interest; omission may lead to tax assessment procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial ownership information update, if reportable particulars have changed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry through the French business formalities one-stop shop
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after a change requiring an update; France does not impose a routine annual beneficial-ownership confirmation solely because a year has passed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file accurate, complete, or timely information may result in criminal penalties for the company and responsible individuals, including fines and, for individuals, possible imprisonment.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SAS must appoint a statutory auditor when it exceeds at least two of these thresholds at the relevant financial year-end: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Separate rules may apply to groups, controlled entities, or regulated activities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French statutory accounts are prepared under French GAAP and the French Accounting Standards Authority (ANC) regulations. IFRS is generally relevant to consolidated accounts of listed groups, not ordinary SAS standalone statutory accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No general annual UBO confirmation is required solely due to the passage of time. File an update within 30 days of a change to reportable beneficial ownership information. Record share transfers and resulting ownership changes in the company records and assess whether an RBE update is required.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders (registre des mouvements de titres and individual shareholder accounts, as applicable)
Minutes and written decisions of shareholders and other competent corporate bodies
Statutory accounting records and supporting documents, retained for 10 years

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 300–1,200 per year, depending on location and service scope; France has no general annual registered-agent renewal fee.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000–10,000 or more per year when a statutory audit is required; actual fees depend on size, complexity, and activity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (Impôt sur les Sociétés, CGI Article 219) applicable to French-resident SAS entities for fiscal years opened on or after 1 January 2022
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 15% on the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit per full 12-month period for qualifying SMEs; research tax credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure; innovation tax credit (CII) at 20% for SMEs; no territorial tax holiday available for scrap metal trading; standard depreciation and deduction rules apply under the CGI

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (Déclaration de résultat) with the full liasse fiscale (forms 2050 to 2059-G), delivered electronically through the EFI / GEDI e-filing portal or the EDI tax transfer system used by the DGFiP
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return due within 3 months of fiscal year-end; for a fiscal year closed on 31 December, due on 3 May of the following year (or the next business day if 3 May falls on a non-working day); non-calendar fiscal year entities must file by the 3rd month following the closing date

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross turnover, exclusive of VAT, from the sale of goods including recycled scrap copper wire and associated commission or freight income; export sales and intra-community deliveries are included before deduction of intercompany offsets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies with a French permanent establishment (PE) report only turnover attributable to the PE; non-residents without a PE enter nil and are not subject to Form 2065 filing for French-source passive income, which is instead subject to withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box GF / Box 111 (Résultat comptable et résultat fiscal)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss taken from the income statement (form 2052), adjusted for fiscal reclassifications, including non-deductible expenses, depreciation, provision addbacks, and transfer pricing corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident PE must compute French-source business income on a separate-entity basis using arm's length attribution of profits; intra-group purchases of scrap copper wire must be documented under the OECD authorised approach.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses carried forward from previous fiscal years, applied against current-year taxable profit; the annual offset is capped at EUR 1 million plus 50% of taxable profit exceeding EUR 1 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses actually booked in the French PE are deductible; foreign head-office losses cannot be set off against the PE's French taxable income unless the DTA permits PE-specific aggregation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 120 / Box 124 (Impôt sur les sociétés dû)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amount of corporate income tax liquidated after applying the standard 25% rate, the reduced 15% SME tranche, loss offsets, and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident PEs, quarterly instalment payments (form 2571) are paid through the appointed tax representative; the balance is settled with the annual Form 2065 liquidation by the statutory deadline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing of Form 2065 triggers an automatic 10% penalty (majoration) on the assessed tax, rising to 40% if the return is not filed within 30 days following a formal written demand, and to 80% in cases of bad faith, abuse, or fraudulent intention; late-payment interest (intérêts de retard) accrues at 0.20% per month from the normal due date; a minimum penalty of EUR 100 applies for each omitted ancillary schedule; the DGFiP may also publish the sanction and impose enforcement measures on bank accounts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% withholding tax (retenue à la source) on dividends distributed by a French SAS to non-resident companies under CGI Article 119 bis; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for EU/EEA corporate shareholders holding at least 10% for an uninterrupted 24-month period; reduced DTA rates (commonly 10%-15%) apply to residents of treaty partners such as China.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The beneficial owner must obtain an official tax residence certificate (attestation de résidence fiscale / TRC) from its resident tax authority, complete Form 5000 (or Form 5001 for corporate shareholders), and submit both to the French paying SAS before the dividend payment so that the reduced treaty withholding rate is applied at source; where the reduced rate was not applied, the non-resident may claim a refund from the French tax administration within the ordinary limitation period, generally by 31 December of the second year following the distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: domestic withholding under CGI Article 182 B is 33.33% for payments to non-residents for IP or know-how used in France, 66.66% for payments routed to non-cooperative jurisdictions; the EU Interest & Royalties Directive (2003/49/EC) grants 0% withholding for related EU companies; most French DTAs reduce patent and technical royalty rates to 10% or 0%. Interest: French-source interest paid to non-resident lenders is generally exempt from domestic withholding unless the beneficiary is established in a non-cooperative state, where a 75% rate applies; treaty protection further limits or eliminates French interest withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000: a French SAS must prepare and maintain the Transfer Pricing Master File and Local File under CGI Article L. 13 AA when its annual French turnover (CA HT) or the consolidated turnover of the group exceeds EUR 50 million; the simplified transfer pricing declaration (Form 2065-SD) is likewise required above that threshold, and all documentation must be provided to the DGFiP within 30 days of a formal request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute as in the UAE, but substance and commercial rationality are enforced through the abuse-of-law rule (Article L. 64 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales), the general anti-abuse rule, the Principal Purpose Test under the BEPS Multilateral Instrument (Article 29), and the requirement that treaty and EU directive benefits are granted only to genuine economic operators with local personnel, premises, and decision-making capacity; artificial shell arrangements are disregarded and recharacterized.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate concealment or false declaration of taxable profits from recycled scrap copper trading, including fictitious supplier invoices, inflated inventory write-offs, hidden cash proceeds, or repeated under-reporting of export revenues.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanction under CGI Article 1741: fine up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years, extended to EUR 2,000,000 and 7 years in aggravated or organised circumstances; the fiscal administration additionally reassesses the tax base with a 40% bad-faith penalty or 80% fraudulent-conduct penalty, plus late-payment interest at 0.20% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the président of the SAS who participate in the fraud are personally exposed to criminal fines and imprisonment; the corporate veil is pierced through solidarité fiscale, allowing seizure of personal assets; travel bans may be imposed pending criminal investigation, and the court may impose the interdiction de gérer (ban on managing commercial enterprises).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File Tax Returns and Liasse Fiscale
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission of Form 2065 or the 2050-2059-G schedules, late filing, or failure to deliver transfer pricing documentation within 30 days of a DGFiP request.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Taxation d'office of the corporate income tax base by the administration; automatic 10% penalty, increased to 40% if the return is filed within 30 days after formal notice, and 80% in cases of fraud; late-payment interest at 0.20% per month; minimum EUR 100 fine per missing schedule.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the company is insolvent and the omission is deliberate, the président may be subject to a personal monetary claim for the unpaid corporate tax; criminal liability for intentional non-compliance may result in fines, imprisonment, and a ban on conducting business activities.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Manipulation and Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling shredded scrap copper wire to a related foreign buyer or shell conduit at non-arm's length prices, mispricing processing margins, shifting customer contracts or trading intangibles abroad without value recognition, or failing to maintain the mandatory local file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Rectification under CGI Article 57: the DGFiP re-determines French taxable profit at arm's length; the upward adjustment is subject to a 40% penalty for serious mispricing, rising to 80% for abuse of law, plus late interest; the recharacterization may convert the excess into a constructive dividend subject to 25% withholding tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving the intercompany pricing policy face joint and several liability for the reassessed tax, penalties, and interest if the arrangement is held to be artificial; criminal prosecution for tax evasion can include personal imprisonment and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abuse of Law / Shell Company and Treaty Shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing or maintaining the French SAS with no real premises, employees, or operational substance solely to access the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, DTA reduced rates, or favourable French withholding treatment on scrap metal trading profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of the abuse-of-law procedure: the transaction is disregarded, benefits are denied retroactively, income is recharacterized at the French statutory 25% rate with a 25% hidden-distribution withholding tax, and an 80% abuse penalty applies on the tax avoided, together with late interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The président and beneficial owners who knowingly maintain the artificial structure are personally liable for the reassessed tax and penalties through the solidarité mechanism; they may be subjected to faillite personnelle (personal bankruptcy), interdiction de gérer, and criminal sanctions including imprisonment and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and AML Violations in Physical Scrap Trading
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving or settling scrap copper wire consignments in cash or structured payments to circumvent the EUR 10,000 anti-money laundering declaration threshold, using forged sourcing documents, or failing to file suspicious transaction reports with Tracfin for circular metals trading.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties under the French Monetary and Financial Code (Articles L. 561-1 et seq.): individual offenders face up to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to EUR 1,000,000; corporate entities face fines up to EUR 5,000,000, asset confiscation, and disqualification from certain business activities; failure to report to Tracfin additionally triggers administrative sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the effective beneficial owner of the SAS are personally exposed to criminal conviction, fines, confiscation of personal assets, freezing orders on bank accounts, and travel bans preventing departure from French territory while under judicial examination.
